mainTopic: Conditions and exclusions in a גט: when a written condition or an excluded man makes the divorce invalid
overview: The amud opens by finishing אביי's view. רבי and the רבנן argue about a condition written in a גט only when it comes before the תורף; after the תורף, everyone says the גט is כשר. רבא flips this: they argue only after the תורף, where רבי makes a גזירה, and before it everyone says פסול. The גמרא fits our משנה to each view. Next, רבי זירא changes a ברייתא that said 'everyone agrees it is פסול' to read 'everyone agrees it is כשר.' The גמרא explains that a reciter can swap כשר and פסול, but would not invent 'דברי הכל.' A new משנה then teaches that a husband may exclude men with whom קידושין cannot take effect, but excluding men with whom it can take effect, even through a forbidden marriage, makes the גט פסול. רבא asks רב נחמן a long series of questions about borderline exclusions. רב נחמן proves that excluding a minor boy ruins the גט. The proofs for the other questions are rejected, and the whole series ends with תיקו. Finally, a new משנה gives the core wording of a גט: 'You are hereby permitted to any man.'

steps.title: After the essential wording, everyone agrees the גט is valid
steps.stepSummary: This finishes אביי's statement: if the condition is written after the תורף, everyone agrees the גט is כשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Everyone agrees it is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing אביי's statement from just before. If the condition is written after the main wording of the גט, nobody, not even רבי, says it is פסול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to אביי, רבי and the רבנן argue only when the condition sits before the תורף. Once the essential divorce wording is already complete, a condition added afterward does not damage the גט in anyone's view.

keyTerms.meaning: The essential wording of the גט that actually divorces her

phrases.english: Everyone agrees that it is valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes אביי's statement from before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to אביי, a condition written after the תורף does not invalidate the גט, and everyone agrees on this.

steps.title: Fitting the משנה into אביי's view in two ways
steps.stepSummary: Our משנה invalidates a written exception but not a written condition. According to אביי, the משנה could be talking about before the תורף and follow the רבנן, or about after the תורף and follow everyone.
steps.simpleTranslation: And our משנה teaches that if he wrote it, the גט is invalid. We explained that this applies only to an exception ('except for'), but a condition ('on condition that') does not make the גט invalid. If you want, say the משנה is talking about before the תורף, and it follows the רבנן. And if you want, say it is talking about after the תורף, and then everyone agrees with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that our משנה fits אביי's view. The משנה says a written condition does not ruin the גט, and the גמרא offers two places that condition could be written.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the גמרא explained that the משנה's 'written = invalid' rule is about חוץ (an exception), not about על מנת (a condition). So the משנה holds that a written condition leaves the גט valid. According to אביי, that is true either before the תורף following the רבנן, or after the תורף, where everyone agrees.

keyTerms.meaning: We established it as referring to a specific case
'Except for': an exception that leaves out a certain man
If you want, say: introduces one of two possible answers

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up חוץ and על מנת. The משנה's 'written = invalid' rule is about an exception (חוץ). A condition (על מנת) does not invalidate the גט according to the משנה.

phrases.english: And our mishnah, which teaches 'he wrote it' (is invalid),
and we established it as dealing with 'except';
but 'on condition' does not invalidate:
if you want, say: before the essential wording, and it follows the Rabbis;

phrases.aramaic: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: לְאַחַר הַתּוֹרֶף, וְדִבְרֵי הַכֹּל.
phrases.english: and if you want, say: after the essential wording, and it is everyone's view.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers a question the reader might ask about the משנה, according to אביי's view in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: Whether our משנה, which does not invalidate a written condition, fits אביי's view.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Two alternative ways to place the case (איבעית אימא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה might seem to contradict רבי, who invalidates a written condition.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is either before the תורף following the רבנן, or after the תורף, where everyone agrees.

steps.title: רבא: the dispute is after the essential wording, because of a protective decree
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the argument is only when the condition is after the תורף. רבי makes a גזירה because of a condition before the תורף, and the רבנן do not. Before the תורף, everyone says it is פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The argument is about a condition written after the תורף. רבי holds that we make a גזירה because of a condition written before the תורף. The רבנן hold that we do not make that גזירה. But if it is written before the תורף, everyone agrees the גט is invalid.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a different picture from אביי, flipping where the argument happens.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבא, a condition before the תורף truly ruins the גט in everyone's view. After the תורף it does not really ruin it, but רבי invalidates it anyway as a גזירה, so people won't confuse it with the before-the-תורף case. The רבנן don't make that גזירה.

keyTerms.meaning: Because of, so as not to confuse it with

steps.whatToRemember: אביי: they argue before the תורף, and after it the גט is valid for all. רבא: they argue after the תורף, where רבי makes a גזירה, and before it the גט is invalid for all.

phrases.english: And Rava said: the dispute is after the essential wording,

phrases.aramaic: דְּרַבִּי סָבַר: גָּזְרִינַן אַטּוּ לִפְנֵי הַתּוֹרֶף;
phrases.english: for Rabbi holds: we decree because of before the essential wording;

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבָּנַן סָבְרִי: לָא גָּזְרִינַן אַטּוּ לִפְנֵי הַתּוֹרֶף.
phrases.english: and the Rabbis hold: we do not decree because of before the essential wording.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל לִפְנֵי הַתּוֹרֶף – דִּבְרֵי הַכֹּל פָּסוּל.
phrases.english: But before the essential wording, everyone agrees it is invalid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with אביי's placement of the argument.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A condition before the תורף invalidates the גט for everyone. After the תורף, רבי invalidates it as a גזירה, and the רבנן validate it.

steps.title: Fitting the משנה into רבא's view
steps.stepSummary: According to רבא, the משנה, which does not invalidate a written condition, must be talking about after the תורף and follows the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: And our משנה teaches that if he wrote it, the גט is invalid, and we explained that this is only about an exception, but a condition does not invalidate it. That משנה is talking about a condition written after the תורף, and it follows the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא runs the same משנה through רבא's view. This time there is only one way to explain it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבא, a condition before the תורף is invalid for everyone, so the משנה cannot be talking about that case. It must be after the תורף, and only the רבנן validate the גט there, so the משנה follows the רבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: It follows the view of the רבנן

phrases.english: And our mishnah, which teaches 'he wrote it' (is invalid),
and we established it as dealing with 'except';
but 'on condition' does not invalidate:
it is after the essential wording, and it follows the Rabbis.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies רבא's view to the same משנה that step 2 applied to אביי's view.
steps.kashyaTarget: Whether our משנה fits רבא's view.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Places the case in one specific situation (אוקימתא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since רבא says a condition before the תורף is invalid for everyone, the משנה might seem to contradict him.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is about a condition after the תורף and follows the רבנן.

steps.title: A ברייתא: everyone agrees a conditional גט is invalid
steps.stepSummary: The father of רבי אבין teaches before רבי זירא that if someone wrote a גט with a condition, everyone agrees it is פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: The father of רבי אבין taught a ברייתא in front of רבי זירא: If someone wrote a גט with a condition, everyone agrees it is invalid.
steps.whatsHappening: A new ברייתא is brought that seems to say there is no argument at all. This sets up רבי זירא's challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ברייתא says 'everyone agrees' a written condition invalidates the גט. That looks like it clashes with the argument between רבי and the רבנן that we have been discussing.

phrases.aramaic: תָּנֵי אֲבוּהּ דְּרַבִּי אָבִין קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי זֵירָא:
phrases.english: The father of Rabbi Avin taught before Rabbi Zeira:

phrases.aramaic: כָּתַב גֵּט עַל תְּנַאי – דִּבְרֵי הַכֹּל פָּסוּל.
phrases.english: If he wrote a get on condition, everyone agrees it is invalid.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנֵי אֲבוּהּ דְּרַבִּי אָבִין קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי זֵירָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new source into the discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A גט written with a condition is invalid, and the ברייתא says everyone agrees.

steps.title: רבי זירא objects: but they argue about this
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא asks how the ברייתא can say 'everyone agrees' when רבי and the רבנן argue about this very case.
steps.simpleTranslation: Everyone agrees it is invalid?! But they argue about it!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא challenges the ברייתא's words 'everyone agrees'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We know רבי invalidates and the רבנן validate a written condition in at least some case. So saying 'everyone agrees it is invalid' seems to erase a known argument, and the ברייתא needs an explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it so that: introduces a challenge

phrases.english: Everyone agrees it is invalid?!
But they do disagree!
phrases.notes: 'They' means רבי and the רבנן, whose argument was discussed earlier.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּבְרֵי הַכֹּל פָּסוּל?! וְהָא מִיפְלָג פְּלִיגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ברייתא just quoted.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's words 'everyone agrees it is invalid'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: We know of an argument between רבי and the רבנן about a written condition, so the claim that everyone agrees cannot be right as it stands.

steps.title: רבי זירא fixes the wording: everyone agrees it is valid
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא changes the ברייתא to say that everyone agrees the גט is כשר, and explains that it is talking about a condition written after the תורף.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, change the wording and say: 'According to everyone it is valid.' And what is the case? When the condition was written after the main part of the גט (the תורף).
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא answers his own question by changing the words of the ברייתא. Now it reads 'everyone agrees it is כשר' instead of 'everyone agrees it is פסול.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem was that the ברייתא said everyone agrees on a case where רבי and the רבנן actually argue. With the new wording, the ברייתא is talking about a condition written after the תורף. In that case, on the view stated earlier in אביי's name, nobody says it is פסול, so 'everyone agrees' really is true.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, say: the גמרא is changing the wording of a source
What is the case? How do we picture it?
The main part of the גט, where it says she is divorced and free to marry

phrases.english: Rather, say:
according to everyone it is valid,
and what is the case? After the תורף.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי זירא's own question from step 6 by changing the ברייתא's wording.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Changing the wording of the source (switching פסול to כשר) and placing the case after the תורף.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא said everyone agrees the גט is פסול, which clashes with the argument between רבי and the רבנן.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא really says everyone agrees it is כשר, and it is talking about a condition after the תורף.

steps.title: Why not fix it to say invalid, following רבי?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי זירא did not fix the ברייתא a different way: keep 'פסול', drop 'everyone agrees', and say it follows רבי.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let him say: 'It is invalid,' and the ברייתא follows רבי!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי זירא's choice of fix. There was another simple way to fix the ברייתא, so why didn't he use it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי holds that a condition makes the גט פסול. So רבי זירא could have kept the word 'פסול' and only removed 'דברי הכל', making the ברייתא follow רבי alone. The question is why he chose to change 'פסול' into 'כשר' instead.

keyTerms.meaning: But let him say: suggests a different reading

phrases.english: But let him say: 'It is invalid'
and it follows רבי!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the specific way step 7 changed the wording.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי זירא's choice to change 'פסול' to 'כשר'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another fix was available that kept 'פסול' and matched רבי's opinion, so why change the ruling itself?

steps.title: Valid and invalid get mixed up, but 'everyone agrees' does not get mixed up
steps.stepSummary: The תנא clearly taught 'דברי הכל'. A reciter can easily confuse 'כשר' with 'פסול', but would not confuse 'הרי זה' with 'דברי הכל'.
steps.simpleTranslation: The tanna taught him 'everyone agrees.' He could mix up 'valid' with 'invalid,' but he would not mix up 'it is' with 'everyone agrees.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי זירא's fix. He changed the word that is easy to get wrong and kept the words that are hard to get wrong.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When fixing a source, you change the part most likely to be a mistake. 'כשר' and 'פסול' are a simple pair of opposites that a reciter could swap. But 'דברי הכל' is a distinct phrase that nobody would add by accident in place of 'הרי זה', so it must be the original wording.

keyTerms.meaning: The reciter who memorized and taught ברייתות
It gets mixed up for him; he confuses it

steps.whatToRemember: רבי זירא's final reading: everyone agrees that a condition written after the תורף does not make the גט פסול.

phrases.english: The tanna taught him 'everyone agrees';
phrases.notes: He means the reciter clearly said these exact words to רבי זירא, so they can't be dropped.

phrases.english: 'valid' with 'invalid' he could confuse,

phrases.aramaic: ״הֲרֵי זֶה״ בְּ״דִבְרֵי הַכֹּל״ לָא מִיחַלַּף לֵיהּ.
phrases.english: 'it is' with 'everyone agrees' he would not confuse.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains which word is more likely to be a mistake.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Dropping 'דברי הכל' and keeping 'פסול' would be just as good a fix.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'דברי הכל' is too distinct to be a mistake, so the word to change is 'פסול'.

steps.title: Excluding men she could never marry anyway: the divorce is valid
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה: if the husband frees her to marry anyone except his father, her father, his brother, her brother, a slave, a non-Jew, or anyone with whom קידושין cannot take effect, the גט is כשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he says: 'You are permitted to every man, except to my father, or your father, or my brother, or your brother, or a slave, or a non-Jew, or anyone with whom she cannot have קידושין,' the גט is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins about a husband who gives a גט but leaves out certain men. Here every man he leaves out is someone she could never be married to anyway.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With these men, קידושין would not take effect at all. So the husband's exception holds nothing back from her, and the גט still frees her completely. That is why it is כשר.

keyTerms.meaning: You are permitted to marry any man: the key words of a גט
Halachic betrothal that creates a marriage bond

phrases.english: MISHNA:
'You are hereby permitted to any man,
except to my father'; or 'to your father';
'to my brother'; or 'to your brother';
to a slave; or to a non-Jew;

phrases.aramaic: וּלְכׇל מִי שֶׁאֵין לָהּ עָלָיו קִדּוּשִׁין –
phrases.english: or to anyone with whom she has no קידושין,
it is valid.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲרֵי אַתְּ מוּתֶּרֶת לְכׇל אָדָם אֶלָּא לְאַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the discussion of the ברייתא ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Excluding men with whom קידושין cannot take effect does not harm the גט; it is כשר.

steps.title: Excluding men she could marry, even through a forbidden marriage: the divorce is invalid
steps.stepSummary: If he excludes marriages that are forbidden but would still take effect, such as an אלמנה to a כהן גדול, a גרושה or חלוצה to a כהן הדיוט, a ממזרת or נתינה to a regular Jew, or a Jewish woman to a ממזר or נתין, the גט is פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he says: 'You are permitted to any man, except a widow to a כהן גדול, a divorcée or חלוצה to a regular כהן, a ממזרת or נתינה to a regular Jew, a Jewish woman to a ממזר or נתין,' or he excludes anyone with whom she can have קידושין, even if it is a sin, the גט is invalid.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the opposite case. Here the men he leaves out are men she could really become married to, even though the marriage would be forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In these forbidden marriages the קידושין still take effect, even though they are a sin. So the husband is truly holding back part of her freedom, and a גט that does not fully free her is פסול.

keyTerms.meaning: A regular כהן, not the כהן גדול
A woman freed from יבום through the חליצה ceremony
A woman born from a forbidden union
A woman descended from the גבעונים
Through a sin; a forbidden marriage

steps.whatToRemember: The test is whether קידושין would take effect. Excluding men where it can't take effect leaves the גט כשר. Excluding men where it does take effect, even forbidden ones, makes the גט פסול.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the second list is valid because these marriages are forbidden anyway. Forbidden is not the same as impossible: these marriages still take effect, so the exception really limits her.

phrases.english: 'You are hereby permitted to any man,'
except a widow to a High Priest;
a divorcée or a חלוצה to a common priest;
a ממזרת or a נתינה to an Israelite;
an Israelite woman to a ממזר or a נתין;

phrases.aramaic: וְכׇל מִי שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהּ עָלָיו קִדּוּשִׁין,
phrases.english: or anyone with whom she has קידושין,
even through a transgression,
it is invalid.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲרֵי אַתְּ מוּתֶּרֶת לְכׇל אָדָם אֶלָּא אַלְמָנָה לְכֹהֵן גָּדוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The contrasting second half of the משנה begun in step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Excluding men with whom קידושין do take effect, even through a forbidden marriage, makes the גט פסול.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the key rule that a גט must fully free the woman. Any exception that truly limits whom she can marry ruins it.

steps.title: What the two general phrases in the משנה add
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the general phrase in the first clause adds all other כריתות, and the general phrase in the second clause adds all other לאוין, like עמוני and מואבי.
steps.simpleTranslation: GEMARA: The general phrase in the first part comes to include all the other relations punished by כרת. The general phrase in the last part comes to include all the other relations forbidden by a לאו, such as an Ammonite and a Moabite (a נתין, an Egyptian and an Edomite).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by explaining why the משנה added general phrases after its lists of examples.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first list (father, brother, and so on) is only examples. 'Anyone with whom קידושין cannot take effect' brings in every other כרת relation, and in all of them the גט is כשר. The second list is also only examples. The general phrase there brings in every other לאו relation, where קידושין does take effect, so excluding them makes the גט פסול.

keyTerms.meaning: Forbidden relations punished by כרת, where קידושין does not take effect
Relations forbidden by a negative commandment, where קידושין still takes effect
An Ammonite or Moabite convert, who may not marry a Jewish woman

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two clauses. With כרת relations קידושין fails, so excluding them changes nothing and the גט is כשר. With לאו relations קידושין works, so excluding them really limits her and the גט is פסול.

phrases.english: GEMARA
The general phrase of the first clause
phrases.notes: This is 'or anyone with whom קידושין cannot take effect' from the first case.

phrases.english: comes to include the rest of those punished by כרת.
The general phrase of the last clause
comes to include the rest of those forbidden by a לאו,
such as an Ammonite and a Moabite
(a נתין, an Egyptian and an Edomite).
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the words in round brackets. A נתין was already listed in the משנה.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּלָלָא דְּרֵישָׁא לְאֵתוֹיֵי שְׁאָר חַיָּיבֵי כָרֵיתוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the wording of the משנה quoted in steps 10 and 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה's general phrases extend its rule to all כרת relations (גט כשר) and all לאו relations (גט פסול).

steps.title: Excluding a minor boy: does it count?
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks רב נחמן what happens if the husband excludes a קטן, who cannot do קידושין now but will be able to when he grows up.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא asked רב נחמן: if he says 'except for a קידושין with a minor boy,' what is the law? Do we say that right now, at least, he is not able to do קידושין? Or perhaps, since he will grow into being able to do קידושין, it counts?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא raises a new question that the משנה's two categories do not clearly answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קטן fits neither box cleanly. Today his קידושין fails, like the כרת cases, which would make the גט כשר. Tomorrow it will work, like the לאו cases, which would make it פסול. The question is whether we judge him by now or by what he will become.

keyTerms.meaning: Someone with whom קידושין can take effect
He will come to be someone with whom קידושין works

phrases.english: Rava asked Rav Nachman:
'Except for betrothal to a minor boy': what is the law?
Do we say that now, at least,
he is not someone with whom betrothal works,
or perhaps he will come to be able to betroth?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the משנה's כשר/פסול distinction to a borderline case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a person who cannot do קידושין now but will be able to later counts as 'בר הויה' for this rule.

steps.title: רב נחמן cites the minor girl divorced from her father's קידושין
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן answers from a ברייתא: a קטנה can be divorced even when her father did the קידושין for her.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: You already learned it. A minor girl can be divorced from a קידושין done by her father.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן brings a source he says already answers רבא's question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case does not look connected at first. A קטנה cannot accept her own קידושין, yet the ברייתא says she can receive a גט. The next steps show why that teaches us about the קטן.

keyTerms.meaning: You learned it, it is already taught
A betrothal her father accepted on her behalf

phrases.english: He said to him: You learned it:
A minor girl can be divorced from her father's betrothal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's question by bringing a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: That someone who will become able to do קידושין counts as able now.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא: קטנה מתגרשת בקידושי אביה.

steps.title: Why can she get a גט if she cannot accept קידושין?
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן asks how the ruling about the קטנה makes sense, since the פסוק links divorce to marriage and she cannot marry by herself yet.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why is that so? Don't we need 'and she leaves' to be like 'and she becomes,' meaning divorce has to match marriage?
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן asks a question on his own source to show what hidden idea it rests on. This sets up the punchline in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק places leaving through a גט right next to becoming another man's wife, so the two are compared. A קטנה cannot accept קידושין herself now. So how can she accept a גט? This is not a real attack. It shows the ברייתא must hold a principle that answers it.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And she leaves... and she becomes': the פסוק comparing divorce to marriage

phrases.english: Why?
But don't we require:
'And she leaves' to be like 'and she becomes'?
phrases.notes: דברים 24:2. Since the two are in one פסוק, divorce is compared to marriage.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the ברייתא from step 14 in order to bring out its principle.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא that a קטנה can be divorced.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Divorce is compared to marriage. She cannot marry by herself now, so she should not be able to be divorced either.

steps.title: Someone who will become able counts as able now
steps.stepSummary: The answer is that the קטנה will grow into being able to accept קידושין, so she already counts as able. The same is true of the קטן, so excluding him makes the גט פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it must be that she will come to be able to marry, and that is enough. Here too, the minor boy will come to be able to marry.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן finishes his proof and applies it to רבא's question about the קטן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא must hold that future ability counts as ability today. Otherwise the קטנה could not receive a גט. Apply that to the קטן: he counts as someone with whom קידושין works. So excluding him is like excluding a לאו case, and the גט is פסול.
steps.whatToRemember: A person who will become able to do קידושין is treated as able now. If a husband excludes a minor boy from his גט, he has really limited her, and the גט is פסול.
steps.confusionAlert: The answer is the second side of רבא's question. Even though the boy cannot marry today, excluding him still ruins the גט.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets a broad idea: future ability (אתי לכלל הויה) counts as present ability when we compare divorce to marriage.

phrases.english: Rather, she will come to be able to be betrothed;
here too,
he will come to be able to betroth.
phrases.notes: So excluding the boy counts as a real limit, and the גט is פסול.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָתְיָא לִכְלַל הֲוָיָה הָכָא נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the question of step 15 and applies the answer to רבא's question in step 13.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Maybe we judge only by the present, so the קטנה cannot be divorced and excluding a קטן changes nothing.
steps.terutzMaskana: Future ability counts now, so excluding a קטן makes the גט פסול.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: אתי לכלל הויה counts as בר הויה. 'Except for a קטן' invalidates the גט.

steps.title: What if he excludes men who are not born yet?
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks whether a גט is valid if the husband lets her marry anyone except men who will be born in the future.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the husband says "except for those who will be born," what is the law? Do we say that right now they are not born, so the exclusion means nothing? Or do we say they are going to be born, so he is really holding back men she will be able to marry?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא asks a new question that follows the pattern of the קטן case. Can a husband exclude men who do not exist yet?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קטן already exists and will grow into someone who can marry, so excluding him ruins the גט. Here the men do not exist at all yet. The question is whether we judge only by today, or also by what will surely happen later.

keyTerms.meaning: Except for those who will be born
They are going to (in the future)

phrases.english: "Except for those who will be born": what is the law?
Now, at least, they have not been born,
phrases.notes: The letter in square brackets is part of the corrected wording. It just makes the word plural: "they."

phrases.english: or perhaps they are going to be born?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the idea that a future ability counts (from the קטן case) and tests how far it goes, to men who are not yet born.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does excluding men who will be born in the future make the גט פסול, or does only the present situation count?

steps.title: A proof attempt from the slave and the gentile in the משנה
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן tries to prove from the משנה that only the present counts. An עבד or נכרי might convert someday, yet excluding them is fine.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: You already learned this in the משנה, "except to a slave and to a gentile" (and the גט is valid). If future possibilities counted, a slave and a gentile can also convert! Yet the גט is still valid.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן tries to answer רבא from the משנה. Excluding an עבד or a נכרי does not ruin the גט, even though they could convert and later be able to marry her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The logic is: if possible future changes counted, excluding an עבד or נכרי should ruin the גט, because they might convert. Since the משנה says the גט is valid, it seems we only look at the present. If so, excluding unborn men should also be fine.

keyTerms.meaning: You have learned it (it is already taught)
If it is so (if your idea were true)

phrases.english: He said to him: You learned it:
"To a slave and to a gentile."
phrases.notes: The משנה says that if he excludes these men, the גט is still valid.

phrases.english: If it is so,
a slave and a gentile are also likely to convert!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to settle the question in step 17 using the משנה.
steps.raayaObject: That only the present situation counts, so excluding unborn men does not ruin the גט.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's ruling that excluding an עבד or נכרי leaves the גט valid, even though they might convert.

steps.title: Rejected: converting is not expected, but being born is
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. An עבד or נכרי is not set to convert, but people are naturally set to be born.
steps.simpleTranslation: Those people (the slave and the gentile) are not standing ready to convert. These people (the unborn) are standing ready to be born.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רב נחמן's proof. It shows that the two cases are not the same.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עבד or נכרי converting is only a possibility. There is no reason to expect it, so we ignore it. Babies being born is the normal course of the world, so it is like the קטן who will surely grow up. That means the משנה gives no proof, and רבא's question stays open.
steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא does not say unborn men count as men she cannot marry. It only says the עבד/נכרי case cannot prove it, because a likely future and a far-off maybe are different.

phrases.english: Those are not standing ready to convert,
these are standing ready to be born.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 18.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from the משנה, not רבא's question itself, which stays unanswered.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof treats a mere possibility (converting) the same as something expected to happen naturally (being born).

steps.title: What if he excludes her sister's husband?
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks about excluding her sister's husband. She cannot marry him now, but she could if her sister dies.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he says "except for your sister's husband," what is the law? Right now she is not fit for him, so maybe the exclusion is fine. Or perhaps sometimes her sister dies, and then she becomes fit to marry him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא asks another question in the same series. This time the excluded man exists, but she is forbidden to him for now.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A woman may not marry her sister's husband while the sister is alive. That is a כרת prohibition. But if the sister dies, he becomes permitted to her. So the question is whether a possible future permission makes him count as someone she could marry, which would make the גט פסול.

phrases.english: Except for her sister's husband: what is the law?
Now, at least, she is not fit for him,
or perhaps sometimes her sister dies
and she becomes fit for him?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new question in רבא's series. It tests whether a forbidden relationship that might later become permitted counts as a future ability.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does excluding the sister's husband make the גט פסול because he might become permitted, or is it valid because he is forbidden now?

steps.title: Proof from the slave and the gentile for the sister's husband
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן tries to answer רבא's question about the sister's husband from the משנה. The משנה allows excluding an עבד or a נכרי, even though they might convert someday and become permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: You already learned this in the משנה: 'except to a slave or to a gentile' is a valid גט. A slave and a gentile can also convert someday, and still excluding them is fine.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן answers רבא's question from Step 20 by pointing to the משנה's case of an עבד and a נכרי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עבד or נכרי cannot marry her now, but they could become permitted if they convert. Since the משנה says excluding them is fine, רב נחמן argues that we only look at the present. So the sister's husband, who is forbidden to her now, should also be fine to exclude.

keyTerms.meaning: You learned it already (in the משנה)
A non-Jewish slave, who cannot marry a Jewish woman

phrases.english: He said to him: You learned it:
"to a slave or to a gentile,"
and a slave and a gentile also
are likely to convert!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's question about the sister's husband using the same proof that was tried in Step 18.
steps.raayaObject: Excluding the sister's husband should not ruin the גט, because only the present counts.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה allowing a husband to exclude an עבד or נכרי, who could convert in the future.

steps.title: Conversion is rare, but death is common
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. Conversion does not happen often, but death happens all the time.
steps.simpleTranslation: Conversion is not common, but death is common.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רב נחמן's proof from the עבד and נכרי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We do not expect an עבד or נכרי to convert, so the משנה can ignore that possibility. But a sister dying is a common thing. So the sister's husband might count as someone she could marry. That makes the two cases different, so the proof fails, and the question stays undecided (see step 31).
steps.confusionAlert: This looks like the same answer as Step 19, but it is a new case. There the point was about men who will be born; here it is about the sister dying.

phrases.english: conversion is not common,
death is common.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in Step 21.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole comparison between the עבד/נכרי and the sister's husband.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Conversion is rare, but death is common, so the sister's husband is likely to become permitted while the עבד and נכרי are not.

steps.title: Holding back only relations outside marriage
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks a new question. What if the husband lets her marry anyone, but says she is still not free for זנות?
steps.simpleTranslation: If he says 'you are permitted to any man except for your licentiousness,' what is the law? Do we say that he did not hold anything back about marriage? Or perhaps he did hold something back, about relations?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא opens a new question about a husband who frees her fully for marriage but not for relations outside marriage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: She can marry anyone at all, so in terms of marriage nothing is held back. But he left her still 'married' when it comes to זנות. The question is whether that counts as holding back part of the גט, which would make it פסול.

keyTerms.meaning: He left something out (held back part of the divorce)

phrases.english: "except for your licentiousness": what is the law?
phrases.notes: He means she may marry anyone, but she is still not free to be with a man outside of marriage.

phrases.english: with regard to marriage, he did not leave anything out,
or perhaps he did leave something out, with regard to relations?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new question in רבא's series, now about holding back only זנות.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does holding back only relations outside marriage count as holding back part of the גט?

steps.title: Proof from 'my father and your father'
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן proves from the משנה's case of 'my father and your father.' Since they can never marry her, that case must be about זנות, and only for them is it fine.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: You learned it: 'to my father or to your father.' What is this about? If it is about marriage, can my father and your father marry her at all? Rather, it must be about relations outside marriage. So only with my father and your father has he not held anything back, but with another man, he has held something back.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן answers רבא's new question from a case in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her father-in-law and her own father can never marry her, because קידושין with them does not take effect. So the משנה's exclusion of them must mean זנות. The משנה allows it only because they are forbidden anyway, which implies that holding back זנות from any other man would ruin the גט.

keyTerms.meaning: People who are able to marry her

phrases.english: He said to him: You learned it:
"to my father or to your father."
phrases.notes: The husband says this while giving the גט, and the משנה says it is valid.

phrases.english: And with regard to what?
If you say with regard to marriage,
are my father and your father able to marry her?!
Rather, is it not about licentiousness?
And it is only with my father and your father that he did not leave anything out,
but with another man, he did leave something out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's question from Step 23 with an inference from the משנה.
steps.raayaObject: Holding back זנות from an ordinary man counts as holding back part of the גט.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה allowing 'except to my father or to your father,' which must be about זנות, implying it is fine only for men already forbidden to her.

steps.title: Maybe it is about a forbidden marriage
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. The משנה could be about marriage, where the father breaks the rule and marries her anyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps it is about marriage, where he transgressed and married her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רב נחמן's proof from 'my father and your father.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof assumed the משנה had to be about זנות, since the fathers cannot marry her. But the משנה might mean a 'marriage' that the father goes ahead with even though it is forbidden. Then the משנה teaches nothing about זנות, so רבא's question is still open.
steps.whatToRemember: Both proofs in this section fail. Excluding the sister's husband is different from excluding an עבד or נכרי because death is common, and the question of holding back only זנות is left unproven.

phrases.english: Perhaps it is about marriage,
where he transgressed and married her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in Step 24.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The reading that the משנה of 'my father and your father' must be about זנות.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה can be read as being about a forbidden marriage that the father goes through with anyway, so it teaches nothing about זנות.

steps.title: Except for intercourse in an atypical manner
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks about a גט that frees her for everything except relations שלא כדרכה. Is the divorce complete?
steps.simpleTranslation: If he says 'except for relations in an atypical manner,' what is the law? Should we say that for normal relations he held nothing back, so the גט works? Or maybe the פסוק says 'the lyings of a woman' in the plural, which puts both kinds of relations together, so he really did hold something back?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues from רבא's question about זנות (Step 23) and asks a new one. This time the husband holds back only relations שלא כדרכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Side one: normal relations are fully free, so maybe nothing that matters was held back. Side two: the plural word משכבי teaches that both kinds of relations count as one thing. If so, holding back one kind is like holding back part of the relationship, and the גט is incomplete.

keyTerms.meaning: Relations in an atypical manner (not the normal way)
He did not leave anything out
Or perhaps (introduces the other side of the question)
'The lyings of a woman,' a plural phrase in the פסוק

phrases.english: Except for relations in an atypical manner, what is the law?
Do we say that for normal relations he did not leave anything out,
or perhaps 'the lyings of a woman' is written?
phrases.notes: ויקרא 20:13. The word is plural, so it teaches that both kinds of relations count the same.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds a new version of רבא's question after the proof about זנות was rejected in Step 25.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does holding back only relations שלא כדרכה count as leaving out part of the divorce?

steps.title: Except for canceling your vows
steps.stepSummary: Is the גט complete if he frees her to marry anyone, but her new husband will not have the power of הפרת נדרים?
steps.simpleTranslation: If he says 'except for canceling your vows,' what is the law? Should we say that for marriage he held nothing back? Or maybe the פסוק says 'her husband may keep it and her husband may cancel it,' which shows that canceling vows is part of being a husband?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks the same kind of question again, now about הפרת נדרים. The husband lets her marry anyone, but her new husband will not be able to cancel her vows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Side one: she can fully marry, so the גט seems complete. Side two: the פסוק ties הפרת נדרים to being 'her husband.' If a future husband cannot cancel her vows, then he is not fully her husband, and the divorce left something out.

keyTerms.meaning: A husband canceling his wife's vows
He may keep it (let the vow stand)

phrases.english: 'Except for the canceling of your vows,' what is the law?
Do we say that for marriage he did not leave anything out,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִלְמָא ״אִישָׁהּ יְקִימֶנּוּ וְאִישָׁהּ יְפֵרֶנּוּ״ כְּתִיב?
phrases.english: or perhaps 'her husband may keep it and her husband may cancel it' is written?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same pattern as Step 26, applied to a husband's power over her vows.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is a husband's power to cancel vows a basic part of marriage, so holding it back ruins the גט?

steps.title: Except for eating תרומה
steps.stepSummary: Is the גט complete if he frees her to marry anyone, but if she marries a כהן she may not eat תרומה?
steps.simpleTranslation: If he says 'except for your eating תרומה,' what is the law? Should we say that for marriage he held nothing back? Or maybe the פסוק says 'bought with his money,' which shows that a כהן's wife eats תרומה because she is fully his, so holding that back makes the marriage incomplete?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks the same kind of question a third time. This time it is about a כהן's wife eating תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Side one: she can marry anyone, so the גט seems complete. Side two: the פסוק says a כהן's wife eats תרומה because she is 'bought with his money,' meaning she belongs to his household. If she could not eat, her marriage to a כהן would not be a full קנין, so the divorce left something out.

keyTerms.meaning: The holy portion of produce given to a כֹּהֵן, which his household may eat
'Bought with his money': someone who fully belongs to the כֹּהֵן's household

phrases.english: 'Except for your eating תרומה,' what is the law?
Do we say that for marriage he did not leave anything out,
or perhaps 'bought with his money' is written?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same pattern as Steps 26-27, applied to eating תרומה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is a wife's right to eat her כהן husband's תרומה part of the marriage itself?

steps.title: Except for inheriting from you
steps.stepSummary: Is the גט complete if he frees her to marry anyone, but her future husband will not inherit from her?
steps.simpleTranslation: If he says 'except for your inheritance,' what is the law? Should we say that for marriage he held nothing back? Or maybe the פסוק says 'to his relative… and he shall inherit her,' which teaches that a husband inherits his wife as part of being married?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks another question in this series. This time her future husband will not be treated as her husband for ירושה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Side one: she can marry anyone, so the גט seems complete. Side two: the פסוק calls the wife her husband's close relative (שאר) who he inherits. If he cannot inherit her, he is not fully her husband, so the divorce left something out. None of these questions gets an answer; step 31 closes them with תיקו.
steps.whatToRemember: These questions (steps 26 to 29) follow one pattern. The husband frees her to marry, but holds back one thing. The question is whether a פסוק makes that thing a basic part of marriage. If it does, holding it back makes the גט incomplete. Step 30 adds one more question of the same kind.

phrases.english: 'Except for your inheritance,' what is the law?
phrases.notes: He means: your future husband will not inherit from you.

phrases.english: Do we say that for marriage he did not leave anything out,
or perhaps 'to his relative' and 'he shall inherit it' are written?
phrases.notes: במדבר 27:11. Here the 'relative' is read as his wife, so a husband inherits his wife.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Final question in the series of Steps 26-28, applied to a husband's inheritance.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is a husband's right to inherit his wife part of the marriage itself, so holding it back ruins the גט?

steps.title: A divorce that excludes betrothal by document
steps.stepSummary: Is a גט complete if the husband frees her to marry anyone, except that a new husband may not marry her through a שטר?
steps.simpleTranslation: If he says, 'You are free to all, except for your betrothal by a document,' what is the law? Do we say that since another man can still marry her with money or with relations, the divorce works? Or perhaps the פסוק joins 'and she departs' to 'and becomes,' so all the ways of becoming a wife are linked to each other?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks one more question in רבא's series. This time the husband holds back only one of the three ways to get married: marriage by document.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One side says she is still free to marry anyone, because money and relations still work, so the break looks complete. The other side reads 'וְיָצְאָה' and 'וְהָיְתָה' together. The leaving must match the 'becoming,' and all three ways of becoming a wife are a set. So holding back even one of them means she has not fully left.

keyTerms.meaning: Betrothal done by handing the woman a document
Money, one of the three ways of betrothal
Relations, another of the three ways of betrothal
'And she departs... and becomes' (the wife of another man)
Are compared or linked together because of the פסוק

steps.confusionAlert: The husband is not limiting who she may marry. He is limiting how a new husband may marry her. Every man is still allowed; only the document method is blocked.

phrases.english: "Except for your betrothal by a document" — what is the law?
Do we say: since it is possible to betroth her
with money and with relations, the divorce works;
or perhaps, since "and she departs" is next to "and becomes,"
the ways of becoming a wife are linked to each other?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a fifth question to רבא's series about partial limits in a גט.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does holding back only one method of betrothal make the separation incomplete, or is the גט still valid?

steps.title: The questions stay unresolved
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא ends the whole series of questions with תיקו: the questions stand without an answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let it stand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא ends all of these questions with one word. It has no proof either way, so the questions stay open.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תיקו here covers every question in this series whose proof was rejected, not just the last one. That means unborn men (step 17), the sister's husband (step 20), זנות (step 23), and the questions in steps 26 to 30. None of them gets a clear ruling, so each case stays in doubt. Only the קטן question (step 13) was actually answered.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Let it stand': the question is left without an answer

steps.whatToRemember: Except for the קטן, which רב נחמן proved makes the גט פסול, all the questions in this series stay unresolved. That covers the unborn, the sister's husband, זנות, relations not in the usual way, הפרת נדרים, תרומה, inheritance, and קידושי שטר.

phrases.english: Let it stand.
phrases.notes: This closes every question in the series that was left without a proof, not only the last one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the series of questions without deciding them.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: All the unanswered questions in the series stay unresolved: the unborn, the sister's husband, זנות, and the partial-limit cases. Only the קטן question was settled (גט פסול).

steps.title: The core wording of a divorce document
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה teaches the essential words of every גט: 'You are hereby permitted to any man.'
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: The core of a גט is: 'You are hereby permitted to any man.'
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It teaches the key sentence that makes a document into a גט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everything the גמרא has discussed about limits on a גט is now tied to this core phrase. The words 'לְכׇל אָדָם' (to any man) show why limits are a problem. A real גט must free her to everyone.

keyTerms.meaning: The core, essential wording of a divorce document

steps.whyThisMatters: This sentence is the basic wording of every גט. Any limit added to it raises the question of whether the divorce is complete.

phrases.english: MISHNA: The core of a bill of divorce is:
"You are hereby permitted to any man."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the series of questions ends with תיקו.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The essential wording of a גט is 'הֲרֵי אַתְּ מוּתֶּרֶת לְכׇל אָדָם'.
